A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 24 complete pages including Appendices A–G. Text and visual comparison establish that pages 2–24 are identical; first-page differences are limited to an author-name correction and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original ASR-ICL experiments on five tabular datasets in Section 6, including binary and multi-class results in Tables 1–2, supplementary analyses in Appendix F, and a case study in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments in Section 6 and Appendices F–G, including quantitative recourse performance, robustness and sensitivity results, and the case study.

M1.justification: ASR-ICL's objective, adaptive subspace selection, importance updates, RACOS optimization, and feasibility projection are identical in Section 5 and Appendices B–C, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Australian Credit, COMPAS, Diabetes, Corporate Rating, and Student Performance. Binary and multi-class tasks, context variations, and target-class scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: DiCE, Actionable Recourse, and FACE remain in Table 1, and Full ZO remains in the efficiency analyses and case study. The evaluated predictor sets are also identical.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain identical evaluation metrics, context settings, feasibility constraints, decoding procedures, and optimization settings, including the default 150-query budget.

E4.justification: Context-size and resampling analyses, query-efficiency comparisons, feature-concentration analyses, hyperparameter sensitivities, context-ordering robustness, target-class sensitivity, and the Diabetes case study are unchanged.

E5.justification: Mean and standard-deviation reporting, plotted uncertainty, and the description of independently resampled contexts are identical. Neither version adds or revises run-count, seed, or statistical-testing information.

E6.justification: All result tables, plots, and qualitative findings are identical. For example, Table 1 retains TabPFN-2.5's Australian Credit validity of 1.00 ± 0.00 and average cost of 3.83 ± 0.04; appendix results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A contain identical mathematical definitions, assumptions, feasibility propositions, optimal-recourse derivations, convergence bounds, and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, theoretical feasibility and convergence, query efficiency, sparsity, and multi-class applicability claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications concerning context length, dimensionality, predictor-dependent sensitivity, and target-class difficulty are unchanged in Sections 4.4 and 6 and Appendix F.

D1.justification: Implementation details, pseudocode, hyperparameters, dataset descriptions, feasibility rules, evaluation pipeline, and prompt template in Appendices B–E are identical. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the paper's positioning relative to prior recourse and tabular ICL research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page author name changes from 'Shaopneg Fu' to 'Shaopeng Fu,' matching the spelling already used in the acknowledgements. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; body prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp is repositioned within the margin. All figures, tables, captions, and remaining page layouts are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects an author-name typo and updates the arXiv stamp. These limited administrative edits leave the scientific exposition, methods, proofs, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
